intro:
# Exercise electrodermal dynamics: persistence survives physiological challenges

The coherent aerobic subset contains30participants with wrist electrodermal activity (EDA), temperature and accelerometry. Six people are reserved, including both linked S11 recording segments;24 people develop models in five whole-person folds. Source4Hz EDA is in microSiemens, temperature in Celsius, and accelerometer units are converted using the source1/64g convention.

## Task and equation

Every five seconds after120seconds of observed history, the task predicts mean EDA over seconds25–30 ahead. The development-selected reference is

$$\widehat E_{[t+25,t+30]}=\overline E_{[t-5,t]}.$$

The rule has no fitted parameters. Each sensor's own start timestamp and sampling rate determine alignment; recording breaks are never bridged. Device-clock dates are timing coordinates, not evidence of a particular measurement calendar year. Signed finite EDA is retained as released rather than silently clipped or excluded.

Five hypotheses tested tonic relaxation, damped drift, preceding activity, thermal change and asymmetric rising/recovery dynamics. Every extension was fitted only on training people with whole-person validation and identical observed-history access. The apparent physiological coefficients failed to improve the strong persistence control.
interpretation: Reserved participant-balanced MAE is0.4902uS for persistence, versus1.1230uS linear extrapolation and0.5420uS flexible prediction. This is useful bounded forecasting evidence and a negative result for the tested physiological extensions. It is not a new sweat-production law, a mental-stress classifier or a clinically validated wearable. Source exercise cadence changes and disconnections are preserved; the single protocol does not isolate temperature, autonomic activity and motion causally. Six held people warrant per-person error reporting, not narrow population confidence intervals.
summary: Five substantive attempts completed; persistence remains selected with0.4902uS reserved-person MAE. More elaborate physiological-response candidates fail to establish incremental transfer.
lessons: Do not treat manufacturer-derived physiological labels as independent sensor truth. Align by each native sensor clock/rate and keep split recording segments under one person. Distinguish physical EDA units from the psychological interpretation of EDA. A long-horizon forecasting task still needs persistence and modest trends as controls. Preserve source signed values and protocol deviations. Do not infer sweat-rate constants from predictive regressors.

findings.claim: Causal EDA persistence transfers to held participants better than registered drift/flexible controls
findings.scope: Thirty source participants within aerobic protocol; six held people
findings.prior_art: Established persistence baseline for slow physiological state
findings.falsification: No new exercise setting, stress diagnosis or clinical tolerance validated

findings.claim: The tested relaxation,activity,thermal and asymmetric-response extensions do not establish transferable physiological gains
findings.scope: The five explicit candidate equations and source protocol
findings.prior_art: Known EDA physiology may exist even when these predictors fail
